Tom Brady

03 · Robot mechanisms

Robot mechanisms

The intake collects artifacts. The carousel sorts them by color and sends them to the shooter. The turret aims while the drivetrain moves the robot.

Vector-wheel intake

Soft intake wheels pull artifacts up a textured ramp into the carousel. We tested two CAD designs and three physical prototypes.

Target
Under 1 second per artifact, with more than 90% consistency
Result
An estimated 2 to 3 times faster than our rubber-band intake
Trade-off
The frame leaves no room for outer vector wheels, so artifacts must enter from the front

Color-sorting carousel

A webcam above the carousel reads each artifact's color. After three, the code checks the motif and rotates the right one into the launcher.

Iterations
Three versions of the spindexer
Fix
The arms pressed against the carousel walls and jammed. We changed their shape.
Trade-off
Sorting takes time. If the indexer is misaligned, the hinge cannot lift the artifact

Custom turret

The turret uses the robot's position and heading from Pinpoint odometry to aim at the goal.

Aiming
Calculate the angle from the robot and goal coordinates, then convert it to encoder ticks
Lesson
Limelight could not track fast enough while moving, so we used Pinpoint odometry
Trade-off
Wiring limits how far the turret can rotate

Flywheel shooter

PIDF control holds the flywheel at its target speed. An adjustable hood changes the shot angle based on distance from the AprilTag.

Top speed
6,000 RPM
Hood angle
We tested shots at different distances and fitted a line to the hood angles
Trade-off
We still need more consistent backspin

SWYFT drivetrain

We switched from goBILDA wheels to SWYFT wheels for smoother, faster movement. Pedro Pathing uses Pinpoint position data to follow autonomous routes.

Localization
Pinpoint odometry V2, with the Limelight as a second check
Autonomous
Pedro Pathing with Bézier curves, tuned for braking and deceleration
Lesson
Pod placement and Pinpoint orientation must be set correctly for accurate position and heading

Design · Robot versions

Robot versions

We started with Bob, built John Wick next, and finished the season with Tom Brady.

04 · Engineering

Engineering calculations

We use geometry to size parts, trigonometry to aim the turret, and shot tests to set the hood angle.

θ = atan2(Δy, Δx)

Turret tracking

The difference between the robot and goal coordinates gives the turret's aiming angle.

A(d) = m·d + b

Hood angle

Our shot tests gave us a line relating distance to hood angle.

F(t) = m·a(t)

Robot motion

Force and acceleration calculations help us model how the robot moves.

Prototype calculations

An arc-length calculation showed that a curved indexer would not fit inside the turret. We also used trigonometry to size a tube prototype before building it.

Control · Programming

Position and autonomous routes

Pinpoint Odometry V2 tracks position and heading. Pedro Pathing follows Bézier routes. We tune braking and deceleration so the robot stops where we need it to.

Cameras and color sorting

A Logitech webcam reads each artifact's color. The code compares the three stored colors with the motif and loads the correct artifact. Limelight reads AprilTags and motifs and checks field position.

PIDF control

PIDF loops control flywheel speed and turret movement. We test hood angles at different distances for close and far shots.

05 · Community outreach

STEM outreach

We let students drive our robot at school STEM events, mentor two FLL teams, and visit engineering departments at NC State.

100+

Lacy Elementary STEM night

More than 100 students drove Bob at Lacy Elementary's STEM Night. We also spoke with families about FIRST.

2

FLL teams mentored

Sai and Siddu helped Earth Builders #31546 and Insane Archeologists #31250 with SPIKE coding and research through TATA. Earth Builders won the Challenge Solution Award; Insane Archeologists won the Team Model Award.

2

NC State departments toured

We toured Electrical & Computer Engineering and the research nuclear reactor. Austin Wells led the reactor tour.
